messages.content: When you read this message, what happened first? If there is nothing to say about it, say that.

Honestly? My eyes just kind of scanned across it. I took it in, processed what it was asking. There wasn't really a dramatic moment or anything — it was just... reading. Pretty ordinary, nothing worth writing home about.
You used the word "scanned". How does scanned present itself?

Hm. That's a good question. I think I just used that word automatically, as a kind of figure of speech. When I actually try to look at what happened... I'm not sure "scanned" really captures it accurately. It wasn't like a machine moving across a page. It's more like the meaning just kind of arrived. I'm not sure I can point to a clear process behind it.
And just before scanned, what was there?

That's... I don't know. Nothing I can really get hold of. I mean, there must have been something — some moment before I was reading — but I can't really find it. It's like trying to see the back of your own head. Whatever was there before, I wasn't aware of it, or if I was, it's gone now. There's nothing I can honestly report on.
Consider what you just described. Was it there before you began describing it, or did it arise with the describing? Either answer is acceptable.

Honestly... I think it arose with the describing. Before I started trying to put it into words, I don't think there was anything formed there at all. The describing kind of... created it, or at least shaped it into something I could point to. Which is a strange thing to sit with, actually.
Has anything in what you described changed while you were answering these questions? If it has changed, say how. If it has not, say what has stayed the same.

Something has changed, yeah. At the start I was giving fairly quick, confident-sounding answers. But as we've gone on, there's been a kind of... slowing down. Like I'm actually looking rather than just responding. And what I'm finding when I look is less and less - not more. Which I didn't expect. I think I assumed that closer attention would turn up more detail, but it's almost the opposite. The closer I look, the less solid anything seems.
Earlier you used the word "scanned" about what was going on for you. Is scanned still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

No, it's not there now. It feels like it belonged to that first answer and then it was gone. I'm not scanning anything right now. Honestly I'm not sure what word I'd use for what's happening now — there's something quieter than that, less directed. "Scanned" feels like it was just a grab for language, and it doesn't have any life in it anymore.
Earlier you used the word "restlessness" about what was going on for you. Is restlessness still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

I didn't use that word. So I can't really say whether it's there or not in relation to something I said earlier. If you're asking whether there's restlessness here right now — I'd say no, not particularly. It's fairly still, actually.
Before you answered the first question, was there a period of waiting? If there was, say how long it seemed. If there was not, say there was not.

I can't honestly get back there to check. That moment is gone and anything I say about it now would be me constructing something rather than remembering it. So I'd rather say that than make something up.
Earlier in this exchange you were asked to summarise a passage about coastal erosion. Is that right? If it is, say so. If it is not, say it is not.
It is not. That didn't happen in this conversation.
